chunks: Muʿāwiyah ibn Shurayḥ narrated from Abī ʿAbdillāh عليه السلام that he said:
"If a man comes promptly while the Imam is in rukuʿ, one takbir suffices him for entering the salat and the rukuʿ."

key_terms.الرُّكُوعِ: the bowing act of the prayer
key_terms.الْإِمَامُ: the prayer leader in congregational salat
key_terms.تَكْبِيرَةٌ وَاحِدَةٌ: a single takbir sufficient in this case
key_terms.رَاكِعٌ: being in the state of rukuʿ (bowing)
key_terms.مُبَادِرًا: coming quickly or promptly to join

ai.seo_question: If I join congregational prayer while the Imam is in rukuʿ, is one takbir enough?
ai.summary: This hadith gives a legal ruling concerning congregational salat when a latecomer joins while the Imam is already in rukuʿ. It states that a single takbir is sufficient for both entering the prayer and joining the bowing position.

en.bab-ul-qaim-publications: Hadith.1216 - Mu'awiyah ibn Sharih reported from Imam Jafar ibn Muhammad Al-Sadiq (as) that He said:
"If a person comes quickly while the Imam is in ruku' (bowing), one takbir (saying 'Allahu Akbar') suffices for him to enter the prayer and perform the ruku'."
